competences: The learner defines by-laws and describes why communities use them.
The learner states duties of local councils in maintaining peaceful communities.
languageCompetence: Learners read and write by-law, local council, community, disputes, order and security.
objectives: By the end of the lesson learners should explain the meaning of by-laws.
By the end of the lesson learners should name at least three reasons why local councils make and use by-laws.
priorKnowledge: Learners know village and district councils from the previous two lessons on decentralisation.
materials: Chart of village local council responsibilities
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls local-council activities and asks learners "What name is given to the laws made by the local councils?". They use pupils' responses to introduce the meaning of by-laws made in village and district councils.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall local-council duties, answer the teacher's opening question and identify rules they have heard about in the community.

steps.content: By-laws are laws made by local councils. Local councils make laws for their local communities. Local councillors help to maintain village order. Local leaders implement government policies.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the textbook facts under "Meaning of by-laws" and explains "By-laws are laws made by local councils. Local councils make laws for their local communities." They ask "State any one role performed by the chairperson on the LC I executive committee." and guide pupils to explain how the council maintains community order.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the sourced content, state the local-council duties and copy the teaching points clearly into their exercise books.

steps.content: By-laws help settle disputes among people. They help promote order in society. They are used to promote peace and security. They promote respect for people's rights.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the textbook facts under "Importance of by-laws" and explains "By-laws help settle disputes among people. They help promote order in society." They ask "How is the LCI vice chairperson useful to children in your community?" and guide pupils to explain how the council maintains community order.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the sourced content, state the local-council duties and copy the teaching points clearly into their exercise books.

steps.content: Local councils settle disputes among neighbours. Local councils maintain law and order. They implement government policies such as immunisation. They promote sanitation within the village. They protect community members and their property. They unite different people within villages. They give information on government programmes.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the textbook facts under "Duties of local councils" and explains "Local councils settle disputes among neighbours. Local councils maintain law and order." They ask "How is the Secretary for defense useful on the Local council I committee?" and guide pupils to explain how the council maintains community order.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the sourced content, state the local-council duties and copy the teaching points clearly into their exercise books.

steps.content: What name is given to the laws made by the local councils? | State any one role performed by the chairperson on the LC I executive committee. | How is the LCI vice chairperson useful to children in your community? | How is the Secretary for defense useful on the Local council I committee?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the original source questions, including "What name is given to the laws made by the local councils?" and "State any one role performed by the chairperson on the LC I executive committee.". They supervise individual work, correct wrong definitions and link answers with the taught duties of local leaders.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners attempt the original questions independently, compare written answers with their notes and correct factual mistakes.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher revisits the definition and importance of by-laws and checks understanding through "How is the LCI vice chairperson useful to children in your community?" and "How is the Secretary for defense useful on the Local council I committee?". They provide feedback and assign the fifth sourced question.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the final oral questions, restate one importance of local rules and record the homework question for revision.

assessment: Check source questions "What name is given to the laws made by the local councils?", "State any one role performed by the chairperson on the LC I executive committee.", and "How is the Secretary for defense useful on the Local council I committee?" in learners' books and correct responses using the lesson notes.
homework: Answer the original exercise question: "State any one role played by the district speaker."
